reading.body:
Oracle's most recent annual revenue of roughly $67 billion, reported through May 2026, makes it one of the largest enterprise software companies in this dataset, with AI embedded across ERP, HCM, and SCM product lines rather than offered as a standalone service.

The three MCP entries associated with Oracle's identifier are narrow and specialized: a multilingual tarot application, an agent API discovery tool, and a signed attestation service for agent decisions. None of these directly reflects Oracle's core enterprise AI product, Oracle Fusion AI, which centers on autonomous database infrastructure and business application intelligence. The gap between the flagship product description and the MCP catalog suggests the MCP entries represent third-party or peripheral integrations built on Oracle's ecosystem rather than Oracle's own published capabilities.

The data records 76 regulatory exposures under Texas law, consistent with Oracle's Austin headquarters. It does not cover data center footprint, power consumption, or compute infrastructure, so no connection to grid demand or physical scaling constraints can be drawn from what is here. Use cases are listed as null, meaning the data offers no evidence of specific deployment outcomes.
